{{Top|canon=Triangulation observation area}}
{{Quote|A very nice view it is, too. I'm a little surprised to find such a room aboard a warship.''&raquo;<br />&laquo;''Oh, it's quite functional. Its full name is Forward Visual Triangulation Site Number One. We place spotters here during combat to track enemy vessels and other possible threats, and to coordinate some of our line-of-sight weaponry.''&raquo;<br />&laquo;''Don't you have sensors to handle that?''&raquo;<br />&laquo;''Of course. And usually they're quite adequate. But I'm sure you know there are ways of misleading or blinding electronic eyes. Sometimes the eyes of a Chiss are more reliable.|translated=1|[[Jorj Car'das]] and [[Force Commander]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]]|<ref name="OF">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref>}}
The '''forward visual triangulation site''' was the name given to any of several large viewports found aboard [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]]<ref name="VotF">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref> and [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] warships.<ref name="OF" />

On Imperial ships, this room was used primarily to perform line-of-sight weaponry targeting in circumstances where the ship's main [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] were knocked off-line.<ref name="VotF" /> On Chiss ships, Chiss warriors were placed in each viewport during a battle in order to track enemy vessels and coordinate the firing of weaponry during combat. The efforts of these Chiss warriors augmented the ship's existing sensor systems, and sometimes provided a more reliable description of a battle.<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] avoided the bustle of the signing ceremony for the [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty]] by sharing a cup of [[Hot chocolate/Legends|hot chocolate]] in the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] [[Chimaera/Legends|''Chimaera's'']] forward visual triangulation site.<ref name="VotF" />
